published_statement: NOT re-read this stage. As the tree records it (massform.py:1054-1070, marked READ by an earlier stage and unverified here): 'At the quantum level these currents are no longer conserved due to the triangle anomaly ... Therefore, one expects that fermion numbers ... are not conserved in any process where the gauge field evolves in such a way that N[A] != 0 ... Namely, Delta N_F^(i) = N[A]' (eqs. (2.2)-(2.4)); and 'where the factor 1/3 comes from the baryon number of a quark, while the factor 3 . 3 is due to colour and number of generations. So, the amounts of non-conservation of baryon and lepton numbers are related: Delta N_e = Delta N_mu = Delta N_tau = (1/3) Delta B ; (B - L) is conserved while (B + L) is violated' (eqs. (2.4)-(2.5)).
published_hypotheses: Hypotheses as the physics requires them. They are derived here, not read from the source this stage:
Standard Model fermion content: N_f complete generations of left-handed SU(2) doublets (Q with 3 colours and baryon number 1/3, and L), plus SU(2) singlets that do not couple to W.

The triangle (ABJ) anomaly of the fermion-number currents in an SU(2) gauge background with topological (Chern-Simons) number change N[A]. The count is one zero mode per doublet per unit N[A], by the index theorem with 2T(2) = 1.
The source uses massless neutrinos implicitly for per-flavour conservation, given how the tree carries H-FLAV. Not read this stage.
The U(1)_Y part of the anomaly and gravitational backgrounds are not in the quoted passage. Whether the source discusses them was not read this stage.
hypothesis_drift: WEAKENED PROXY (harmless), massform.py:1041-1048 and 518-519. The source's N_f is 'number of generations' of SU(2) doublets. The tree counts N_f as charged leptons in the PDG capture (Q3 = -3). These agree only if generations are complete. rederive (d) shows that SM gauge-anomaly cancellation (Y^3 etc.) and Witten's even-doublet condition hold per COMPLETE generation, and that a partial generation spoils U(1)_Y^3. So the proxy is sound under the SM. The capture gives 3.

DROPPED (incompleteness of H-BL), massform.py:832-833 and 508-510. H-BL says 'B - L is exactly conserved' and names only a Majorana mass as the breaker. rederive (c) computes B - L's mixed gravitational anomaly coefficient, Sum over Weyl fields of (B - L). It is -1 per generation (-N_f) with no nu^c, and 0 with one nu^c per generation. The (B-L)^3 coefficient behaves the same way: -1, or 0 with nu^c. In the nu^c-less SM, 'exactly conserved' therefore needs a second, unnamed hypothesis: vanishing gravitational Pontryagin density, or right-handed neutrinos present. The anomaly EQUATION this coefficient enters, div J = c R Rtilde (Alvarez-Gaume & Witten 1984), is NAMED-NOT-READ here. The coefficient itself is COMPUTED. Its magnitude in any warp geometry is not computed.

DROPPED (wording), massform.py:175-177 ('The only Standard Model violation of B comes from the SU(2) anomaly, with Delta B = Delta L = 3 per unit of Chern-Simons number') and 510-513. rederive (b) computes the U(1)_Y^2 anomaly coefficient of B + L as -1 per generation, the same magnitude as the SU(2)^2 coefficient (+1), and that of B - L as 0. So B + L also changes with the HYPERCHARGE Chern-Simons number (hypermagnetic helicity; Giovannini & Shaposhnikov hep-ph/9710234, NAMED-NOT-READ). That change is not quantised in units of N_f per transition. It is still B - L-conserving, so the tree's B - L balance (N_n extra leptons) is unaffected. Only 'the only violation ... SU(2)' and the integer transition count are route-specific. Whether the source itself names the U(1) term was not read this stage.

CARRIED, NOT DROPPED, massform.py:834-836. H-FLAV (per-flavour conservation, massless neutrinos) is the source-era hypothesis. The tree restricts it to the electron-family sub-count (electron_family_shortfall, massform.py:2158-2162), which carries no verdict. The drift is recorded, and the tree already quarantines it.

The tree's ceil(B/N_F) (massform.py:2125-2127) runs on a float B of about 4.2e28, so the ceil is not meaningful at the unit level (53-bit mantissa). It is a representation note with no effect on any 5-significant-figure figure.

rederivation.outcome: Exit 0, 38 checks PASS, none FAIL. (a) Index-theorem zero-mode count per unit N[A]: Delta B = N_c N_f/3 = N_f at N_c = 3 and Delta L = N_f, so Delta N_e = Delta B/3 = 1 per generation, and the 't Hooft vertex (qqql)^3 carries (B, L) = (3, 3). The source's '1/3' and '3 . 3' factors reproduce. (b) Triangle coefficients per generation: SU(2)^2 gives B 1/2, L 1/2, B - L 0, B + L 1. U(1)_Y^2 gives B -1/2, L -1/2, B - L 0, B + L -1. SU(3)^2 gives B 0. So B - L is anomaly-free under both electroweak factors and B + L is anomalous under both. (c) Gravitational: B 0, L 1, B - L -1 with no nu^c and 0 with nu^c. (B - L)^3 is -1 with no nu^c and 0 with nu^c. (d) SM gauge anomalies cancel per complete generation, and doublets per generation = 4 (even). (e) massform's N_F = 3, transitions 1.4036e28, extra leptons 1.8977e28 = N_n, and THOOFT_DELTA_B_L = (3, 3) all reproduce.

lacked_data: In 1996 the authors lacked the evidence for neutrino mass (oscillations, 1998 onward). Evidence either way: (i) The anomaly selection rule does not use neutrino mass. rederive (a) derives Delta B = Delta L = N_f from the doublet content alone, and the vertex is flavour-basis independent. So having the datum does not change Delta B = Delta L = N_f or B - L's anomaly-freedom under SU(2) x U(1)_Y. (ii) The datum does falsify per-flavour lepton conservation, i.e. H-FLAV. The tree already confines H-FLAV to a verdict-free sub-count (massform.py:834-836, 2158-2162). (iii) Whether B - L survives depends on a datum still missing today, Majorana vs Dirac. The tree names this as H-BL. The neutrino-mass datum reshapes H-BL: with Dirac nu^c the gravitational B - L anomaly cancels (rederive (c)), and with Majorana masses B - L breaks by 2 regardless. (iv) N_f = 3 was already fixed by LEP in 1996 and has not moved. No datum the authors lacked moves the conclusion as the tree uses it. M's hypothesis is not borne out for THIS result. That is recorded with the caveat that the source text itself was not re-read this stage.
grade_evidence: The selection rule the tree uses re-derives exactly from SM quantum numbers (rederive (a), (b), (d)): Delta B = Delta L = N_f per unit N[A], Delta N_e = Delta B/3, B - L anomaly-free under SU(2)^2 and U(1)_Y^2. Every figure the tree computes with it reproduces (e). No moved datum moves it. It is NARROWED and not STANDS for two tree-side reasons, both COMPUTED here: (1) H-BL (massform.py:832-833) calls B - L 'exactly conserved' and names only a Majorana mass. In the nu^c-less SM, B - L also has a mixed gravitational anomaly coefficient of -N_f (0 with nu^c; rederive (c)). So exactness further needs vanishing gravitational Pontryagin density or right-handed neutrinos, a hypothesis the tree drops. The anomaly equation this coefficient enters is NAMED-NOT-READ, and no magnitude is computed. (2) massform.py:175-177 says the only SM B violation is the SU(2) anomaly with Delta B = 3 per unit CS number. The U(1)_Y^2 coefficient of B + L is -N_f (rederive (b)), so hypercharge Chern-Simons change also moves B + L, and not in integer steps of N_f. It still conserves B - L. Neither narrowing moves the tree's verdict-bearing statement, which is explicitly conditioned on a B - L-conserving route ('On a B-violating, B-L-conserving route ... it is N_n extra leptons', massform.py:509-510). The narrowing is of the tree's wording of H-BL and 'only', not of Rubakov & Shaposhnikov's rule.
